A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reversal of Thought framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison across relocated and revised material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-4 reasoning accuracies, inference timings, component ablations and human evaluations of cognitive preference consistency.

after.justification: v2 reports original GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-turbo benchmark results, timings and ablations, and retains the human-evaluation findings.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same reverse-reasoning warm-up, preference scoring, knowledge-boundary routing and final prompting procedure. The edited illustrative pseudocode and plug-and-play description do not establish a change to the RoT algorithm.

E1.justification: The eight named tasks remain. Reported Sonnet Writing requirements expand from three mandatory words in v1 Section 4.1 to three or five in v2 Appendix A.1. Results are not separated by variant, limiting comparison of that task's aggregate scores.

E2.justification: Quantitative comparisons retain CoT, Meta-prompting, ToT, GoT and BoT. However, v1 Figure 2 compares CoT's 57.5-minute MGSM answer with RoT's 145-minute answer; v2 retains the RoT solution in Appendix B.2.2 while removing that qualitative CoT comparator.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from GPT-4 alone to GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-turbo across the benchmark comparisons, knowledge-boundary assessment, timings and component ablations. This substantially broadens the model configurations tested. The one-/two-shot settings, warm-up search, similarity threshold and stated evaluation criteria remain.

E4.justification: The same three component-removal analyses are extended to GPT-3.5-turbo. Appendix B.1.2 adds a Game of 24 instantiation for 4, 9, 10, 13, and the preceding pseudocode example is revised. The MGSM worked solution is retained from v1 Figure 2 and reformatted in Appendix B.2.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run variability. Added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds GPT-3.5-turbo benchmark, ablation and timing results and revises many GPT-4 values. Table 1's GPT-4 Game of 24 scores change from 97.5/97.8 to 97.0/98.0 for one/two shots. One-shot Checkmate-in-One without CPM changes from 98.0, above full RoT's 91.8, to 89.2, below full RoT's 91.2. Reported GPT-4 RoT time changes from 6.69 to 6.79 seconds.

T1.justification: The preference-transitivity assumption, preference-scoring mathematics and knowledge-boundary definition remain unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added. Revised timing notation introduces no new mathematical claim.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly frames RoT as a plug-and-play warm-up framework preceding batch inference and emphasizes modularity in place of the introduction's explicit error-resilience contribution. The principal accuracy, efficiency and knowledge-boundary claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 extends the versatility interpretation to GPT-3.5-turbo, and Limitations adds teacher–student distillation as a prospective application. The explanations of insufficient one-shot context, unknown tasks and mitigation through CPM/two-shot demonstrations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds dataset access links, and Appendix B.1.2 supplies an illustrative Python implementation for a worked problem. Existing reverse-reasoning and CPM prompts are relocated rather than newly disclosed; embedding-model, GPU, threshold and warm-up details largely remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and brief discussion covering symbolic tools/solvers, self-refinement, self-reflection, cost-adaptive self-consistency and reasoning boundaries, including Cai, Pan, Madaan, Renze and Guven, Wang, and Chen. Logic-of-Thought and Xiang et al. are also newly cited. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and results discussion receive localized rewrites. Dataset descriptions move into an expanded Appendix A, and Appendix B gains finer subsections. Most motivation, method exposition, conclusion and human-evaluation instructions remain closely matched.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redesigned; accuracy and ablation tables are transposed and grouped by base model; the timing chart becomes paired model bars. The reverse-reasoning prompt moves to a full-width appendix display, and case-study displays expand. These materially restructure the paper's visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Adding GPT-3.5-turbo comparisons and ablations reduces v1's reliance on one base model and checks whether component effects transfer. Clearer architecture presentation, dataset links and worked-example documentation also improve assessability. These gains outweigh limited reporting regressions, including duplicated Table 2 numbering and v2's CPM discussion citing 45.0 for GPT-4 Python Puzzles where the corresponding ablation row reports 40.6.
